name: Assi Ghat
description: The southernmost main ghat, popular with students, backpackers and long-stay travellers for its calmer riverfront, morning aarti, yoga classes and cafes. More laid-back and open than the central ghats, it is a favored base for those wanting Ganges life at a gentler pace.
bestFor: Nomads and students wanting calm riverfront, yoga and cafes

name: Dashashwamedh Ghat
tagline: Main ghat of the grand aarti
description: The most famous and central ghat, site of the nightly Ganga aarti and the spiritual heart of the riverfront. Surrounded by temples, guesthouses and intense activity, it offers the most immersive experience but also the biggest crowds, noise and constant foot traffic.
bestFor: Visitors wanting the iconic aarti and riverfront steps from lodging

name: Godowlia and old lanes
tagline: Bazaar maze behind the central ghats
description: The dense commercial hub just inland from Dashashwamedh, a warren of narrow lanes leading to Kashi Vishwanath Temple and packed with markets, street food and silk shops. Chaotic and vibrant, it is the practical heart for shopping and eating close to the main ghats.
bestFor: Travellers wanting markets, street food and temples in the old core

name: Cantonment (Cantt)
tagline: Leafy modern quarter near the station
description: The former British military district in the north, with wide leafy roads, hotels, the junction railway station and modern amenities. Orderly and green compared with the old city, it suits those wanting comfort, hotels and transport links, though it is away from the ghats.
bestFor: Nomads wanting quiet, hotels and transport away from the crowds
